distinguishing_features: Actively modulates gasket contact pressure with a pneumatic bladder rather than merely monitoring seal leakage
Uses chamber exhaust flow rate as the primary feedback variable for seal re-stressing
Uses vacuum pressure as a secondary signal to select a high-vacuum operating regime
Applies closed-loop real-time gasket preload compensation during high-flow operation
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Maintaining effective seal contact pressure and leakage resistance despite thermal relaxation and flow-dependent operating changes during high-flow vacuum operation.
parsed.viable_reason: The proposed actuation and physics are insufficiently defined and internally inconsistent, while increased contact pressure does not directly suppress permeation through an intact elastomer.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Active exhaust-flow-driven modulation of seal preload is a distinct feedback-actuation concept not directly taught by the cited monitoring and prediction approaches.
